items.title: How directive can you afford to be, given the status gap and the trust you've built?
items.description: L2 said facilitative is the safer default with someone like Jordan, but that it shifts with trust and stakes. This models that shift: as the formal status gap grows, being directive costs more — unless trust between you has grown enough to absorb it. The defaults roughly match Renee's hallway conversation with Jordan (a large status gap, very little built-up trust yet, and Renee choosing a fairly low-directiveness approach). Drag directiveness up to see why she didn't just tell Jordan what to do.

params.name: statusGap
params.label: Formal status gap (0 = equals, 10 = large gap in their favor)

params.name: trust
params.label: Trust built so far in the relationship

params.name: directiveness
params.label: How directive your mentoring approach is

items.compute: const risk = (params.directiveness * params.statusGap * 5) / (params.trust + 1); const receptionScore = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, 100 - risk)); return { receptionScore };

outputs.label: How well the approach is likely to land
